newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Bavaria in split share.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Bavaria in split share.

text.p: Colombian brewing giant Bavaria will propose a share split within the next month as part of a strategic bid to separate its industrial and investment activities, the company's president said Friday.
Augusto Lopez announced the proposed split on the sidelines of Bavaria's annual stockholders' meeting. He said a new meeting would be called within the next month to formalize the proposal.

Bavaria currently has about 280 million shares ordinary shares on the market in Colombia. Lpez was short on details, but said, "There will be 280 million shares corresponding to industrial activity and 280 million corresponding to investment."
The share price of Bavaria, flagship of the Santo Domingo industrial group, has risen by more than 63 percent in dollar terms so far this year.
ING Barings reiterated its buy recommendation on Bavaria Tuesday, saying its price to earnings ratio remains at a discount to the Colombian market and was at half the Latin American sector average.
Barings said its year-end price target for Bavaria was $8.30, which would imply a 25 percent dollar upside.
Lopez declined to specify how much Bavaria would invest in Angola. He said the project would be handled by the company's Portuguese subsidiary Central de Cervejas (Centralcer) .
Bavaria, which Lopez said ranked among the world's top 10 brewers, has subsidiaries in Ecuador and Spain in addition to Portugal.
Bavaria recently entered into a strategic alliance with three Argentine companies in the Pescarmona Group to produce capital goods, including ships and railway infrastructure, Lopez said.
